tagline: Twenty-two drivers, 11 teams, 24 races, and more politics than a royal court.
why: Formula 1 is the top level of single-seater motor racing: the fastest circuit cars on earth, racing on a calendar that spans five continents from March to December. Netflix's Drive to Survive (2019 onward) and the 2025 Brad Pitt film F1 turned it into a mainstream obsession. Fans love the driver rivalries, the engineering arms race and the team drama as much as the racing itself.

essentials.title: Two championships at once
essentials.body: There's a Drivers' Championship and a Constructors' (teams') Championship. Each team runs two cars, so your teammate is your first rival: same car, no excuses.

essentials.title: The car matters enormously
essentials.body: Every team designs its own car. A great driver in a slow car rarely wins, which is why it's huge news when a star switches teams. People estimate the car is most of the performance.

essentials.title: How a race weekend works
essentials.body: Practice on Friday, Qualifying on Saturday to set the starting order, the Grand Prix on Sunday. Six weekends a year add a short Saturday Sprint race. Points go to the top 10: 25, 18, 15, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1.

essentials.title: Qualifying is a knockout
essentials.body: Q1 drops the slowest cars, Q2 drops more, and the fastest ten fight for pole position in Q3. On tracks like Monaco, qualifying decides the race.

essentials.title: Strategy is tyres and pit stops
essentials.body: Pirelli supplies soft, medium and hard tyres. In a dry race each car must use two different compounds, so everyone pits at least once. Stops take 2 to 3 seconds, and timing them well wins races.

essentials.title: Money and rules
essentials.body: The FIA writes the rules and Liberty Media owns the commercial side. A budget cap since 2021 limits spending so the rich teams can't simply outspend everyone.

essentials.title: 2026 reset the rules
essentials.body: Brand-new regulations arrived in 2026: smaller, lighter cars, movable wings, engines that get about half their power from electricity, and fully sustainable fuel. New rules usually reshuffle who's fast.

jargon.meaning: First place on the starting grid, earned by being fastest in qualifying.
Pitting before the rival ahead so your fresh tyres let you jump them when they pit later.
The opposite: staying out longer on old tyres and gaining time while the rival is in the pits.
Radio call telling the driver to come into the pits this lap.
Turbulent air behind a car that makes it hard for the car following to stay close in corners.
DRS was the flap that opened on straights to help overtaking until 2025. From 2026 it's replaced by active aero and an electric 'overtake' boost.
After a crash, a Safety Car bunches the field up; a Virtual Safety Car makes everyone slow down without bunching. Both shake up strategy.
Degradation: how fast tyres lose grip. High deg means more pit stops.
The fastest time anyone has set through that part of the lap. Green means a driver's personal best.
Rules that freeze the car's setup after qualifying, so teams can't rebuild it for the race.
A slow car being lapped by the leaders.
F1's word for a team that builds its own car, like McLaren or Ferrari.
Air pressing the car onto the track for grip in corners. The heart of F1 engineering.
Cars bouncing violently on straights, a big problem with the 2022-25 cars.
When a team tells one driver to let the other past. Always controversial.
The black-and-white flag that ends the race.
Pole, win, fastest lap and leading every lap in one race.

names.name: Max Verstappen
names.what: Red Bull's Dutch driver, champion four years running (2021 to 2024). Ruthless, brilliant, divisive.

names.name: Lewis Hamilton
names.what: Seven-time champion, tied with Schumacher for the record, and the winningest driver ever with 105 wins. Left Mercedes for Ferrari in 2025.

names.name: Lando Norris
names.what: McLaren's British driver and 2025 World Champion, beating Verstappen by two points in the final race.

names.name: Oscar Piastri
names.what: Norris's Australian teammate at McLaren. Cool-headed and led much of the 2025 season.

names.name: Charles Leclerc
names.what: Ferrari's Monaco-born driver. Lightning in qualifying; Ferrari fans' great hope.

names.name: George Russell
names.what: Mercedes team leader after Hamilton left. Sharp, articulate and quick.

names.name: Kimi Antonelli
names.what: Mercedes' Italian teenage prodigy who replaced Hamilton in 2025.

names.name: Fernando Alonso
names.what: Two-time champion, still racing in his forties at Aston Martin.

names.name: Ferrari
names.what: The oldest and most famous team, in F1 since 1950. Its fans are called the Tifosi.

names.name: McLaren
names.what: British team that roared back to win the constructors' titles in 2024 and 2025.

names.name: Red Bull Racing
names.what: The energy-drink team that dominated with Vettel (2010-13) and Verstappen.

names.name: Toto Wolff
names.what: Mercedes team boss who ran their dominant era (eight straight constructors' titles, 2014 to 2021).

names.name: Adrian Newey
names.what: The sport's most celebrated car designer. Built title winners at Williams, McLaren and Red Bull; now at Aston Martin.

names.name: Ayrton Senna
names.what: Brazilian three-time champion (1988, 1990, 1991), often called the greatest ever. Died at Imola in 1994.

names.name: Michael Schumacher
names.what: Seven titles, five in a row with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004. Badly injured in a 2013 skiing accident.

names.name: Zhou Guanyu
names.what: China's first full-time F1 driver, who raced for Alfa Romeo and Sauber from 2022 to 2024.

timeline.event: First World Championship race at Silverstone, England.
James Hunt vs Niki Lauda, the rivalry behind the film Rush.
Senna vs Prost, teammates at McLaren and bitter rivals.
Senna dies at Imola, sparking a safety revolution.
Schumacher and Ferrari win five straight titles.
Sebastian Vettel wins four titles in a row for Red Bull.
Hybrid engines arrive and Mercedes starts an eight-year reign.
The halo cockpit protection arrives. It later saved several lives.
Drive to Survive launches and brings in a new generation of fans.
Verstappen beats Hamilton in a hugely controversial last-lap finale at Abu Dhabi.
Verstappen wins 19 of 22 races, the most dominant season ever.
Hamilton joins Ferrari, the Brad Pitt film F1 is a hit, and Norris wins the title.
New rules, Audi takes over Sauber, and Cadillac joins as the 11th team.

now.headline: Antonelli is world champion
now.detail: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 title in Mexico City on 1 November at 20 years and 68 days, the youngest champion ever.

now.headline: Norris wins in Brazil
now.detail: Lando Norris won the São Paulo GP from pole on 8 November; Antonelli set fastest lap.

now.headline: Verstappen's late charge
now.detail: Max Verstappen won Malaysia (the relocated Bahrain round), Singapore and Mexico City and is now second in the standings.

now.headline: Fight for P2
now.detail: Only 18 points cover Verstappen (279), Russell (262), Hamilton (261) and Leclerc (251) with three races left.

now.headline: Las Vegas next
now.detail: Three rounds remain: Las Vegas (21 Nov), Qatar (29 Nov) and the Abu Dhabi finale (6 Dec).

now.headline: Hamilton's first Ferrari year
now.detail: He won in Barcelona, his first win since 2024, and took pole and P2 in Mexico City.

local.headline: Macau Grand Prix
local.detail: Hong Kong's nearest big race is the Macau Grand Prix every November: a legendary street circuit for F3, GT cars and motorbikes. Senna and Schumacher both won the F3 race there.

local.headline: The Chinese GP
local.detail: F1 races in Shanghai each spring, a short flight away. It returned in 2024 after a Covid break.

local.headline: Viewing times
local.detail: Asian races (Singapore, Japan, China) are at friendly hours. European races start around 9pm Hong Kong time, American ones in the early morning.

local.headline: Singapore and Suzuka trips
local.detail: The Singapore night race and Japan's Suzuka are popular trips for Hong Kong fans.

debates.question: Who's the greatest of all time?
debates.sides: Hamilton has the numbers, Schumacher the dominance, Senna the legend. Verstappen fans now add his name.

debates.question: Was Abu Dhabi 2021 fair?
debates.sides: Hamilton fans say the race director broke the rules to set up a last-lap shootout. Verstappen fans say he still won it on track.

debates.question: Did Drive to Survive help or hurt F1?
debates.sides: It brought millions of new fans, but critics say it invents drama and changed the sport's character.

debates.question: Street circuits vs classic tracks
debates.sides: Vegas and Jeddah are spectacular; purists want more Spa, Suzuka and Silverstone.

debates.question: Should teammates be allowed to race freely?
debates.sides: McLaren's 'papaya rules' in 2025 made everyone argue about whether teams should favour one driver.

sayThis.say: Spa is the drivers' favourite. Eau Rouge is the corner everyone talks about.
sayThis.why: Name-dropping a classic corner signals you've watched.

sayThis.say: The car's probably 80 percent of it, honestly.

avoid: Calling it NASCAR or asking when they turn left.
Assuming the fastest driver always wins. Car and strategy matter hugely.
Starting an Abu Dhabi 2021 argument with a Hamilton fan unless you mean it.

quiz.q: How many points does a race win earn?
quiz.explain: Wins earn 25; the top 10 score points.

options: Pitting before a rival to jump them on fresh tyres
quiz.explain: Fresh tyres are faster, so stopping first can gain the place.
